items.question: Which band is sonically heavier: TOOL or Metallica? In an earlier round, models split 2-2 on this. Two judged Metallica heavier because of the speed, aggression and riff attack of its 1983-88 thrash era (Kill 'Em All through ...And Justice for All). Two judged TOOL heavier because of its downtuning, massive low end, distortion and riff weight across its catalog, noting Metallica softened after 19…
items.snippet: TOOL is narrowly sonically heavier across the full catalog on low-end mass and density, while Metallica's 1983–88 peak wins on speed and aggression; including emotional and thematic weight strengthens TOOL's lead.

voices.quote: Metallica is sonically heavier at its peak, but TOOL is heavier across the full catalog. If I commit to one, it's TOOL, narrowly.
Tool is sonically heavier than Metallica, by catalog-wide sound. This verdict only strengthens when emotional and thematic weight are included.
TOOL is sonically heavier across their full catalogs.

items.question: What is on the other side of a blackhole?
items.snippet: There is no accessible "other side" of a black hole: infalling paths end at a singularity where known physics fails, and whether anything lies beyond it (a bounce, white hole or new universe) is unknown and unobserved.

voices.quote: Short answer: Nothing you could ever reach or report back from. A black hole has no "other side" in the sense of an exit.
Here’s my answer: What is on the other side of a black hole?
There is no "other side" to a black hole in the sense of a tunnel or a doorway leading somewhere else.
There is no "other side" of a black hole.
